verdicts.decision_note: The client defines the persistent NFT metadata schema, but the source does not establish the proposed backend, smart-contract, and storage component assignments.
This is the first explicit implementation claim for dynamic NFT metadata on the Base testnet.
The client specifies that the on-chain referral-code metadata attribute must use the NFT's own mint number.
Removing Big Blocks necessarily removes the previously established Big Block ticket counter from the NFT metadata schema.
The cited clauses define ticket issuance and association with an NFT, wallet, and mint number, not the NFT metadata projection itself.
First concrete wallet-display failure: Rabby showed the NFT without its image or metadata information.
This is a target-specific correction claim for each NFT's referral, ticket, and earnings details.
The source describes aggregate ticket and commission accounting but does not identify an NFT metadata counter; the provisional update overstates and misroutes the evidence.
The client explicitly requires randomly assigned no-code commissions to be displayed in NFT attributes.
The client defines NFT-attribute projection, historical data-repair, and ticket-to-commission consistency requirements for code-used and no-code rewards.
The client removes the historical metadata backfill obligation while retaining prospective attribute correctness; the existing boolean key is validly updated to false.
Distinct layer-specific failure: the leaderboard and NFT header were correct while the NFT attributes remained stale.
Target-specific post-failure claim: the metadata service was changed to use the live on-chain metadata source.
First concrete post-fix verification: the client refreshed after the metadata-source change and confirmed the result was correct.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

execution.observed_behavior: No-code reward data was missing from NFT attributes, and one NFT displayed two tickets but only one corresponding $5 commission.
